items.title: Jeff Riddick Interview, 1983-07-14
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Dick Allen. I guess you should tell yours if it picks you up.

ctx.x: I see. Is it picking my voice up? Oh, good. Then I can tell my name. Dick Allen. I guess you should tell yours if it picks you up.
I don't know if it picks me up. Yes, it does. Yeah. Oh, this is Pam Tyler.

items.title: Jeff Riddick Interview, 1983-08-01
items.q: It has an article in it by Dick Allen.

ctx.x: Mm-hmm. This is the Second Line magazine. Yeah. May 1953. Meet Jaffer.
It has an article in it by Dick Allen.

items.title: Jeff Riddick Interview, 1983-08-01
items.q: And they asked me, the piano player, said I heard her name, Alan something.

ctx.x: Well, when you used to go sit in, you know, just for fun, you didn't drink then, did you?

Yeah. Where would you go to sit in? Who would you like to sit in? Just where you happened to be. Well, last Sunday night, I passed by the Maison Bourbon, but of course I was not drinking at all. And I never had a drink that night, for that matter. But it was Milton Rich's band. And they asked me, the piano player, said I heard her name, Alan something.
I can't think of his name. Very fine piano man.
